slides.title: Heart Walk Staff Interview Research
slides.subtitle:
Prepared for: AHA National Leadership
Prepared by: Live Neuron Labs
Date: February 2026
Sources: Six in-depth interviews across five markets

slides.title: Executive Leadership Team (ELT) Process, Tools & Staff Experience
Executive Summary
slides.content: Heart Walk is a sophisticated, relationship-driven system designed to generate corporate revenue, build executive leadership pipelines, and activate community fundraising.

bodyField.text: Heart Walk is a sophisticated, relationship-driven system designed to generate corporate revenue, build executive leadership pipelines, and activate community fundraising.
bodyField.quoteText: The campaign is strong. The people are committed. The infrastructure is not keeping pace with the complexity.

slides.title: Five Major Realities
slides.content: The findings cluster around five major realities.

bodyField.text:
1. ELT Prospecting Is the Hardest Problem in the Campaign
2. Chair Recruitment Works — But Is Structurally Fragile
3. Tools Exist — But Are Hard to Access, Use, or Trust
4. Staff Are Creating Solutions Nationally — Without Being Asked
5. The External Environment Has Shifted

slides.title: The System Reality: Heart Walk Is a Relationship Engine
Relationship Engine
slides.content: Heart Walk operates through layered relationships.

bodyField.text:
Staff recruit and coach volunteer leaders.
Volunteer leaders recruit companies.
Companies mobilize teams.
Teams recruit walkers.
Walkers are expected to fundraise.

slides.title: Breakdown Points
slides.content: Every breakdown observed in interviews occurs at a relationship handoff point.

bodyField.text: Every breakdown observed in interviews occurs at a relationship handoff point.

slides.title: What’s Working
slides.content: The volunteer connector model is highly effective.

leftField.text:
Staff prepare connectors with:
- Historical giving
- Company data
- Suggested language
- Strategic framing

rightField.quoteText: We rarely get a flat no. The vetting happens before the ask.

bodyField.text:
1-year confirmed pipeline
2-year projection
Occasional 3-year creative pitches
Multi-year pitching expands opportunity windows.

leftField.text:
Thin Prospect Pools
Some markets made “countless asks” to the same 5–8 executives — all declined.

slides.title: Responsibility Misalignment
slides.content: Boot camp teaches chair recruitment is an ED/VP responsibility with DD support.

bodyField.text: In some markets, the DD owns it entirely — without executive-level peer leverage.

Executive-level peers recruit peers.
Payment timing supports long-range strategy.
Markets have mature pipelines.

It breaks when:
Responsibility drops too low.
Policy reduces flexibility.
Prospect pools are shallow.

New seats (3–5 annually): bottleneck.

Primary barriers:
1. Corporate Sponsorship Requirement
2. Timeline Compression
3. Prospect Ownership Constraints
Several markets independently stated:
bodyField.quoteText: Five engaged members are better than fifteen passive ones.

bodyField.text: Across all six interviews:
bodyField.quoteText: ELT members do the first ask. They rarely do the follow-up.

bodyField.text:
Corporate budget tightening
Healthcare funding cuts
Political climate anxiety
Executive bandwidth depletion
Generational turnover in donors

Transparent Accountability
Public Recognition

Behaviorally, this aligns with:
Social eGains (status, recognition)
Reduced social eCosts (fear of embarrassment)

slides.title: Aha Insight
slides.content: ELT engagement is not a tools problem.

bodyField.text:
It is a behavior design problem.

The campaign currently relies on:
Personal initiative
Goodwill
Volunteer motivation

Instead of systematically designing:
Reduced follow-up friction
Increased visibility of progress
Stronger social reinforcement loops
Every interviewee raised SharePoint.

Pipeline visibility
Cross-market account visibility
Contact intelligence

Limitations:
Reporting less intuitive than Tableau
Missing comprehensive campaign snapshot
Data hygiene gaps creating real operational harm

Newer staff:
Overwhelmed
Skim or skip
Not always on distribution

Suggestion raised:
Split into spring/fall editions.

slides.title: Innovation Insight
slides.content: Staff are independently building missing infrastructure.

bodyField.text:
Examples identified:
ELT Member Job Aid (national gap)
Annotated ELT agendas
Executives with Heart one-pagers
OFT email template workflow
Coach coaching newsletters
Custom slide decks
Market-level SharePoint restructuring

slides.title: Aha Insight
slides.content:
Innovation is happening.
It is decentralized.
It is not being harvested.

bodyField.text:
This represents:
Lost efficiency
Redundant labor
Slower learning loops nationally

slides.title: What’s Working
slides.content:
Boot camp: “An A.”
Mission onboarding: strong.
Consultants (especially former field staff): highly valued.

bodyField.text:
One live session during active campaign
No durable retention
PDF guides outperform videos

Onboarding pacing inconsistent:
One staff completed onboarding in four days (allocated 90).
Idle time during highest motivation window.

slides.title: High-Leverage Insight: Peer Mentorship
slides.content: One first-year director described a colleague eight months ahead as:

bodyField.text: One first-year director described a colleague eight months ahead as:

Lead with mission.
Then leadership opportunity.
Then logistics.

Example framing shift:
Instead of:
“Here’s the ELT commitment.”

Start with:
“Do you want to lead something that changes your community?”
